rv: Denmark's only attempt of a horror movie with creatures

This is a movie made in cooperation with American filmstudio and actors, since it was released in two versions, one with English soundtrack and one with Danish soundtrack. I can't find out who dubbed the Danish actors, but they were definitely dubbed.

I'm happy to find a nice print of this film here. Currently this is not the easiest science fiction B-movie to find a decent copy of on the interwebs. Reptilicus takes me back to my youth, and those Chiller Theater or Creature Feature movie nights on television (back even before cable TV was introduced).
Harryhausen Had Nothing to Do With This Movie

Which doesn't mean the effects are poorly done. They're fine. But Kai Koed is the one to thank for the stop motion effects. (Listed as Kaye Koed in the Credits). Ray made a lot of fine films and was a credit to his teacher Willis O'Brien, but he didn't make EVERY movie featuring stop-motion and miniatures and he didn't work on this Danish Production. Four stars for film minus forty-five stars for the jackass who credited it to Harryhausen.

rv: Some good info on life in Ancient Rome, but brief

This is a story of a young slave and his equally young "master." His father actually owns the slave. The film starts to look at the relationship between two such Romans, which is a topic confusing to those of us more familiar with America's version of slavery. But then it ends too soon. I'm no less confused now. I wanted to know more. I wanted a fuller picture of the experiences and outlooks of these young Romans. Still, some interesting factoids. I liked the Latin dialog. Too bad the actors were just dubbed, and didn't speak the Latin lines.
